newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares find local support, but look down.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares find local support, but look down.

text.p: Leading Russian shares dipped on Monday as Western investors focused on Wall Street and traders saw further easing in coming days despite domestic support.

The Russian Trading System 21-share index slipped to 554.20 after closing on Friday at a record 569.23. Oil company Kondpetroleum was dropped from the list of companies included in index calculations effective today as it moved down to the RTS-2 segment for less liquid stocks.
Traders said the market was consolidating after a run of closing record indexes and all-time high prices on many stocks last week.

"The market is stabilising -- in the next two weeks the market might settle a little lower," said one senior Western trader. "Support is still strong but no one is going to grab everything at once anymore."
National power company UES EESR.RTS slipped to close unofficially at $0.4438 after $0.4575, while international long-distance carrier Rostelekom RTKM.RTS fell to $4.93 from $5.05 on Friday.
Rostelekom announced late on Monday that first half net profits slipped to 431.2 billion roubles after 585 billion roubles in the same period last year.
"Clients are basically very calm -- they are neither selling nor buying," the Western trader said. "But bids are mostly in roubles, while offers are mostly Western."

ICFI-Moscow trader Denis Sysoyev said several Russian banks and other domestic investors remained keen to take out equity positions and would take the opportunity to do so with every lowering of prices.
"We are still looking down, but we don't think that the market will fall very much, since any falling off will be considered a good sign to buy," he said.
